stem: Riya keeps a candle 30 cm in front of a convex lens of focal length 20 cm. She takes away the screen and sticks black paper over the top half of the lens. What happens to the image?

options.A: Only half of the candle's image forms, 60 cm behind the lens
options.B: The full image still forms 60 cm behind the lens, only dimmer
options.C: No image forms anywhere, because there is no screen
options.D: The full image forms 12 cm behind the lens, only dimmer

r1.text: Without a screen there is nothing to hold the image, so it doesn't form.

r2.text: Every point of the candle still sends light through the open half, and those rays still meet at 60 cm.

r3.text: The paper blocks the top half of the lens, so that part of the picture is lost.

verify_flags: D uses the sign slip 1/20 + 1/30 = 1/12, giving 12 cm

stem: Arjun's magnifying glass makes a sharp image of the ceiling tubelight on his notebook. A friend's thumb covers the left half of the lens, and Arjun slides the notebook away. What about the image now?

options.A: It vanishes, because the notebook was what made it
options.B: Half of the tubelight's image is missing, at the same spot
options.C: It moves along with the notebook to the new place
options.D: A complete but dimmer image still forms in the air at the same spot

r1.text: Light from every part of the tubelight still goes through the open half and meets at the same spot, page or no page.

r2.text: The thumb blocks half the lens, so half the image goes dark.

r3.text: The image was only on the paper. Take the paper away and it's gone.

verify_flags: Assumes the tubelight is far enough that the image forms near the focus on the same side as the notebook

stem: In the lab, Meera puts a bulb 15 cm in front of a convex lens of focal length 10 cm. Tape covers the lower half of the lens, and there is no screen on the bench. What is true about the image?

options.A: Only the top half of the image forms, 30 cm from the lens
options.B: No image forms until a screen is placed 30 cm from the lens
options.C: A full, inverted, dimmer image forms 30 cm from the lens, twice the bulb's size
options.D: A full, dimmer image forms 6 cm from the lens

r1.text: Tape on the bottom half means the bottom half of the lens can't make its part of the picture.

r2.text: The light needs a screen to land on, otherwise there's no image yet.

r3.text: Rays from each point of the bulb still pass through the top half and cross at 30 cm, screen or not.

verify_flags: D uses the sign slip 1/10 + 1/15 = 1/6, giving 6 cm

stem: At a science fair, a big convex lens forms a real image of a diya in mid-air; there is no screen. A price sticker covers half the lens. Kabir stands well beyond the image and looks back at the lens. What does he see?

options.A: The whole diya, upside down and a little dimmer
options.B: Nothing, since a real image needs a screen to show up
options.C: Only half the diya, because the sticker blocks the rest
options.D: The diya upright and enlarged, like through a magnifying glass

r1.text: The sticker stops light from that half of the lens, so that half of the diya can't reach his eyes.

r2.text: The rays really meet at the image spot and then carry on to his eyes, and each point still gets light through the free half.

r3.text: There's no screen, so the light never forms a picture he can look at.

verify_flags: Assumes Kabir's eye is at least about 25 cm beyond the image and inside the cone of rays leaving it; if the cone misses his eye he sees only the lens lit up
